chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud narrated from Ali ibn Habashi ibn Quniyy from Ja'far ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Sulami from Abd Allah ibn Hammad from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, what do you say about one who neglects the visitation of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) while he is capable of doing so?' He said, 'He has disobeyed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and disobeyed us, and he has belittled a matter that is for him. And whoever visits him, Allah will be for him behind his needs, and he will be sufficient for whatever concerns him from the affairs of his world. Indeed, it brings sustenance to the servant and replaces what he spends, and his sins of fifty years are forgiven, and he returns to his family with no burden or sin upon him except that it has been erased from his record. If he dies on his journey, the angels descend, wash him, and a door to Paradise is opened for him, its spirit entering him until he is raised. And if he is safe, the door through which his sustenance descends is opened for him, and for every dirham he spent, ten thousand dirhams are made for him, and that is stored for him. So when he is resurrected, it is said to him, 'For you, for every dirham, ten thousand dirhams. Indeed, Allah looked out for you and stored it for you with Him.'

key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation (specifically of the Imams or shrines)
key_terms.عَقَّ: To disobey or neglect a duty towards a superior

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards and spiritual benefits of visiting Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), transmitted through the chain of Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the spiritual gravity of Ziyarat al-Husayn is elevated to a covenantal act of obedience, where neglect is equated with 'Qadha al-Nafs' (disobedience) to both the Prophet and the Imams. The text emphasizes a holistic divine recompense, promising the forgiveness of fifty years of sins, angelic burial for those who die during the journey, and a multiplier of ten thousand for every dirham spent, illustrating the concept of *Jaza' al-Amal* (reward for action) in Shia piety.
